revision_reason.diagnosis: The strongest supported failure mechanism is evidential overreach: repeated descriptions of paired slopes are being treated as proof of material rotation. Construction review is also too easily reduced to whether visible pieces appear to meet, followed by generic reassurance. The EliteBook label discrepancy does not justify substituting an unproven construction accusation for an overclaimed orientation finding.
material_revision: Require a comparison of competing rigid groups: product base, tabletop perimeter, and the support's own thickness/frame assembly. Establish which group is internally coherent before attributing a mismatch.

Separate three conclusions: compatible projection or minor obliquity; clear relative rotation between coherent groups; and independently visible support deformation or construction awkwardness. Allow unresolved attribution instead of forcing one defect.

Make paired boundaries necessary supporting evidence rather than an automatic confidence multiplier. Short, shallow or partly occluded boundaries can leave convergence and materiality uncertain even when two edges are named.

Broaden construction assessment beyond impossible joins to clearly malformed overall shape or assembly, while requiring a concrete visible cue. Thick aprons, splayed legs, fitted supports, asymmetry and unfamiliar legal designs are not failures by themselves.

Permit rejection of an allegation because its inference is unsupported, without demanding proof that the entire alternative assembly is correct. Preserve actual occlusion and hidden-member uncertainty.
Keep the use specialist from certifying geometry through statements about suitable support role, accessible controls or a coherent activity.
revision_reason.expected_effect: These changes should reduce the EliteBook-style orientation overclaim without suppressing the stronger Cashmere conflict. They should also improve construction discovery and attribution when genuine shape or assembly evidence exists. They do not guarantee recovery of the EliteBook construction label, which remains unsupported in my present reading.
